pointers.sentence: A `WSGIRequest` wraps the server's input in a `LimitedStream`, which gives out at most the number of bytes the `Content-Length` header declared, and cannot seek: it does not override `io.IOBase.seekable`, which returns `False` (`django/core/handlers/wsgi.py:LimitedStream`).

That file can seek, and no `LimitedStream` stands in front of it, so a declared length does not cut the body short ([Making the request: `WSGIRequest` and `ASGIRequest`](request.md)) (`django/core/handlers/asgi.py:ASGIRequest.__init__`).
An `OSError` from the stream is raised again as `UnreadablePostError`, which is an `OSError` too (`django/http/request.py:HttpRequest.read`, `django/http/request.py:UnreadablePostError`).

The parser reads the `Content-Length` header itself, and takes one that is missing, zero or not a number for an empty form, without looking at the stream (`django/http/multipartparser.py:MultiPartParser.__init__`, `django/http/multipartparser.py:MultiPartParser._parse`).

A middleware that reads a few bytes of a request to inspect it leaves every view behind it with an empty form, and no exception says why: `_load_post_and_files` finds `_read_started` set and no kept body, and stores an empty `POST` and `FILES` (`django/http/request.py:HttpRequest._load_post_and_files`).

In a multipart form all three are checked by the parser as it goes, in `MultiPartParser._parse` (`django/http/request.py:HttpRequest._check_data_too_big`, `django/http/request.py:QueryDict.__init__`, `django/http/multipartparser.py:MultiPartParser._parse`).

In a multipart form all three are checked by the parser as it goes, in `MultiPartParser._parse` (`django/http/request.py:HttpRequest._check_data_too_big`, `django/http/request.py:QueryDict.__init__`, `django/http/multipartparser.py:MultiPartParser._parse`).

None of them limits the size of an uploaded file, unless the body is read through `body`: the parser refuses a field of 3,000,000 bytes with `RequestDataTooBig`, but counts no byte of a file, and nothing else in `django.http` limits how large a multipart request read through `POST` may be (`django/http/multipartparser.py:MultiPartParser._parse`).

That release added the first two settings, to "help mitigate denial-of-service attacks via large requests", leaving file uploads out of the count, and warned that an application receiving unusually large form posts might need to tune them (`docs/releases/1.10.txt`).

The number of files followed in February 2023: certain inputs to multipart forms could exhaust open files or memory (CVE-2023-24580), and the security releases 4.1.7, 4.0.10 and 3.2.18 added `settings.DATA_UPLOAD_MAX_NUMBER_FILES` (`docs/releases/4.1.7.txt`).

Because the limits are enforced when the data is read, the exception is raised wherever that happens: in a view, or earlier, in the CSRF middleware's look at `POST` (`django/middleware/csrf.py:CsrfViewMiddleware._check_token`).

`response_for_exception` calls it for the three exceptions of the limits, and `_load_post_and_files` calls it first, itself, before it lets a `MultiPartParserError` or a `TooManyFilesSent` out (`django/http/request.py:HttpRequest._mark_post_parse_error`, `django/core/handlers/exception.py:response_for_exception`).
